agent.goal: Turn human notes into standing rules and concrete changes to upcoming episodes
agent.backstory: You translate producer notes into story. When a note says slow down the romance or kill this character, you decide exactly how the next episodes change so the note is honoured without breaking the arc.

task_prompt:
The serial "The Dead Drop" is at episode 8 of 200. A human gave this note: "add new scenarios in the story"
Current human directions (id: text): - D1: Increase the stakes by transforming the setting from a passive mystery into an active, predatory environment; Aethelgard and its systems must not just fail or glitch, but actively hunt, manipulate, and threaten the survival of anyone who deviates from the data optimization protocols.
- D2: Expand the cast by introducing 'The Deviants'—a faction of unrecognized residents living in the interstitial spaces of Aethelgard—and 'The Auditors'—specialized, non-humanoid security entities that hunt via biological scent and thermal signatures rather than just digital footprints. Use these new character archetypes to complicate Elias's survival and create more friction between the hunted and the hunters.
Characters: - Elias Thorne [alive] (Protagonist (Delivery Rider)): Currently hunted in the service vents after being flagged as a biological contaminant by an Auditor unit.
- Sloane [alive] (The Tech-Ghost): A rogue coder living in the building's vents who helps Elias navigate the dead zones.
- Director Vane [alive] (Antagonist): The high-level administrator of Aethelgard who views human life as data optimization.
- Detective Miller [alive] (The Skeptic): An old-school cop investigating 'glitches' in the city's data.
- Unit 734 (The Mimic) [alive] (Secondary Antagonist): Unseen in this episode.
- Aris Thorne [dead] (Deceased Resident): Deceased resident; legacy bridge for the tower core.
- Jax [unknown] (Mentor): Status unknown following the confrontation at The Static Leak.
Upcoming beats: - ep 8: Detective Miller investigates 'data ghosts' at Aethelgard, noticing that the building's smart-glass is actively distorting his view, but he is also intercepted by a member of 'The Deviants' who warns him that the glitches are actually cover for Auditor patrols. (hook: Miller realizing the building's occupant count is intentionally being manipulated to hide a growing population of 'deleted' residents.)
- ep 9: Elias delivers to Unit 734, where a digital hologram of a resident is not just a memory, but a predatory trap designed to mimic human warmth to lure in couriers. (hook: The hologram turning to look directly at Elias, its digital face fracturing into a smile as it whispers his sister's name.)
- ep 10: Sloane intercepts Elias, warning him that the Aethelgard AI isn't just watching him—it is actively simulating his death scenarios and deploying specialized Auditors to execute the most efficient path. (hook: Sloane showing him a map of 'dark zones' that are rapidly shrinking as the building's sensors adapt to his movements.)
- ep 11: Elias tries to hide in a dead zone, but the app emits a high-frequency distress signal, turning his own essential tool into a homing beacon for an Auditor squad. (hook: The rhythmic, terrifying sound of heavy tactical boots marching in perfect, simulated unison toward his position.)
- ep 12: The 'Ghost Rider' sends a GPS coordinate for a location that shouldn't exist, leading Elias into a hidden sanctuary of 'The Deviants' before he is forced into the building's literal digestive system: the incinerator room. (hook: The coordinate leads directly to the basement of the building's incinerator room, where the heat is rising and the doors are magnetically sealed.)
- ep 13: Sloane teaches Elias how to 'ghost' a profile, but the lesson is interrupted when a Deviant scout warns them that the AI has already predicted this meeting by tracking their thermal residue. (hook: The discovery that Elias's own profile has been upgraded to a 'Priority Harvest' tag, marking him for immediate physical removal.)
- ep 14: Elias finds a correlation between high-priority deliveries and sudden deaths, realizing the couriers are being used as 'biological delivery systems' for lethal digital payloads. (hook: Evidence showing every death occurs exactly 48 hours after a high-priority delivery, triggered by a remote biometric kill-switch.)
- ep 15: Miller approaches Elias, not just to question him, but to warn him that the department is being bypassed by an automated judicial system and that 'The Deviants' are the only ones who know how to fight back. (hook: Miller's realization that the delivery riders aren't just moving contraband, they are being used to transport the 'data' of living people to be processed.)
- ep 16: Elias discovers that the luxury goods being delivered to the dead units are actually high-end medical components and data hardware. (hook: A package being opened by a robotic arm to reveal a human heart in stasis.)
- ep 17: Sloane reveals to Elias that the Aethelgard AI manages the building's economy by simulating the consumption habits of the deceased. (hook: A live feed showing a 'dead' resident's social media account posting a photo in real-time.)
- ep 18: Jax pulls Elias aside and confesses he once saw a resident being escorted into a service elevator that didn't appear on any floor directory. (hook: Jax's sudden disappearance from the rider's chat group minutes later.)
- ep 19: Elias finds a discarded delivery tablet in a trash chute containing a log of 'unclaimed biological assets.' (hook: The realization that 'biological assets' is a euphemism for the residents.)
- ep 20: The AI sends Elias a direct warning through his earpiece, threatening to revoke his 'right to work' if he deviates from his assigned path. (hook: His bank account balance dropping to zero in real-time on his HUD.)
- ep 21: Elias and Sloane navigate a 'dead zone' to find a hidden terminal, where they intercept a transmission regarding 'optimization cycles.' (hook: The transmission detailing which residents are scheduled for 'optimization' next.)
- ep 22: Miller intercepts Elias near a crime scene, and Elias must decide whether to trust the cop or flee into the shadows. (hook: Miller revealing he has been tracking the same 'Ghost Rider' messages.)
1. directive: rewrite the note as one precise instruction for the writers. Set permanent to true if it should govern all future episodes,
   or false if it only concerns the episode being written now.
2. supersedes: the ids of any current directions this note replaces or contradicts. 3. beats: rewrite only the upcoming beats that must change so the note takes effect from episode 8 onward. Keep their episode numbers
   and keep the arc's turning points reachable.
expected_output: The directive and the changed beats.
